messages:
maria: quick heads-up — seeing steady KV cache memory growth on long chat sessions (2k+ tokens). profiler shows lots of small free fragments + host page faults. link: https://perf.redwood/internal/dash/kv-frag
perf-bot: ALERT: instance i-rc-43 mem-growth > 1.8GB in 18m for model redwood-v1-large (kv_frag_ratio=0.52) :warning:
kevin: can you paste the latest snapshot / sample alloc backtraces?
maria: pasted the minimal snapshot below (sanitized):
```
# kv-mem-snapshot 2026-03-01T12:34Z
total_kv_resv: 8GB
resident: 6.9GB
live_slots: 3.8GB
free_fragments: 4.2GB (count=1_075_000, avg=4KB)
largest_free_run: 64KB
page_faults: 432 -> mostly minor faults
hot_allocators: attention_kv_shard_7, kv_allocator_global
```
```
kevin: that fragmentation profile (many ~4KB holes) screams block-size mismatch + rounding from allocator. we recently changed slab alignment in kernel-selector v2 (8KB->16KB) — might be related.
jake: long-context chat workloads keep KV growing because we keep inserting many small tokens into different streams; eviction runs but leaves tiny holes. compaction looks doable but expensive on the main path.
olga: locking concern: full-heap compaction will stall inference. we should prefer incremental/cooperative compaction per-shard while shard is idle or during batching gaps. think epoch-based scan + try-coalesce strategy.
kevin: quick proto idea: background coalesce thread per shard that scans free-lists and merges adjacent free runs > threshold_size. rate-limit to N pages/sec to avoid IO spikes. Metrics: coalesced_bytes, coalesce_cycles, stalled_requests_during_coalesce.
maria: +1. also propose experiment matrix: (A) reduce allocator block quantum to 4KB for long-context mode, (B) background coalesce with rate-limit, (C) opportunistic compaction when burst queue is empty, (D) telemetry: fragment_ratio, avg_hole_size, largest_free_run and correlate with page_faults.
jake: I can run sim for A/B using the existing allocator sim harness — should be quick. we'll need representative traces (long-chat + multi-tenant mix).
kevin: note: reducing quantum helps fragmentation but may increase metadata overhead and slow fast-path allocation (more list ops). measure latency p50/p99 under load.
olga: alternative: keep current quantum but add a small lookaside cache for tiny allocations (<8KB) that can be coalesced cheaply later. lower lock contention if lookaside is per-core.
maria: action items: 1) jake to run sim for A/B and push results by Tue, 2) kevin to prototype background coalesce sketch (non-blocking) and metrics by Wed, 3) olga to prototype lookaside idea and evaluate contention impact, 4) add a perf dashboard tile for frag_ratio & coalesce metrics.
kevin: small patch idea for immediate mitigation: when free_fragments_count > 500k, trigger opportunistic eviction + lightweight pass to merge runs >= 8KB. not perfect but might reduce short-term page faults.
maria: thanks — syncing 1:30pm PT tomorrow to align experiments. if anyone finds a smoking-gun perf regression tied to selector v2 config, ping here and tag @kevin. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Scheduled report generated: /reports/kv-frag-triage/1791234567 — added to thread.
kevin: noted. I'll add a flag to toggle long-context quantum at runtime for fast rollback.
maria: perfect. I'll create a short RFC with goals + experiment matrix after the meeting.
kevin: thanks all — feel free to add test traces to the sim bucket: s3://redwood-perf/kv-traces/long-context/
